title: Logspace decidability of indexed languages
statement: Let $C$ be a family of directed acyclic circuits that is canonical at every input length and has polynomial size, with its size language, every gate-type language, and its edge language all decidable in logarithmic space. Let $\ell$ be Boolean and let $p(x,i)$ be a predicate on bit strings and natural numbers. Assume that whenever $p(x,i)$ holds, the description string of $C$ on $x$ is nonempty. Also assume that for every $n,i$, the Boolean obtained by taking the disjunction of $\ell$ with bit $i$ of the encoding of the length-$n$ circuit (using false when $i$ is outside the encoding) equals the truth value of $p(1^n,i)$. Then the language of paired encodings of $x$ and the binary representation of $i$ for which $p(x,i)$ holds is decidable in logarithmic space.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a circuit family canonical at every input length
the size language, each gate-type language, and edge language of $C$ are in logarithmic space
$p$ is a predicate on bit strings and natural numbers
if $p(x,i)$ holds, the description string of $C$ on $x$ is nonempty
for every $n,i$, the specified circuit-encoding bit, disjoined with $\ell$, equals the truth value of $p(1^n,i)$
caveat: The supplied formal snippet leaves the definition of the circuit description string blank, so that hypothesis cannot be made more explicit from the given ground truth.
